text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Flood victims in Nsanje and Chikwawa districts have not received relief food for three months prompting some to return to their abandoned homes.
- Fears mounted on Sunday that most hospital staff will join a civil service strike after picketers increased their pressure on people to stay away from work.

- Police in northern Malawi have arrested Civil Servants Trade Union officials as a strike by the civil service entered its third week, Malawi Congress of Trade Union secretary general, Francis Antonio, said on Sunday.

- The opposition Alliance for Democracy (AFORD) and Malawi Congress Party (MCP) said they had agreed not to Field candidates in by-elections in seven constituencies in areas where their opposition was popular.

- Malawi Congress of Trade Union (MCTU) leaders on Sunday claimed the government had instructed police to arrest any union officials trying to encourage a civil service strike. Agriculture Minister Mapopa Chipeta however dismissed the allegatios as "bizzare and most stupid".
- Uncertainty hangs over the country's three referral hospitals in Blantyre, Lilongwe and Zomba hit by a civil service strike.
- Mozambique authorities have intensified their search for the killers of a British couple, Andrew and Carolyn McDown, who were murdered near the Malawi border post last week.
- The Electoral Commission is to spend 20 million kwacha for the seven by-elections scheduled for May 22.
